config.objection_1: a reviewer argued the orientation and single-bold filters may select against tables that report uncertainty, because dispersion-bearing cells are harder to parse, which would bias the headline upward
config.objection_2: a reviewer argued that papers contributing no parsed comparison are scored as printing no error bar, inflating the paper-level absence rate
config.test: measure the error-bar rate in discarded versus retained tables, and trace which table set the paper-level statistic actually reads

notes: Both objections are answered against themselves. The filter selects for tables with error bars, not against: retained tables carry one at 21.2 percent and discarded tables at 11.7, so the headline is conservative rather than inflated. And error-bar detection reads every detected table rather than only those reaching the comparison stage, so 107 papers with tables but no comparison are correctly credited; only the 235 papers with no detected table at all are scored blind.
